label: Root links from Stephan Leuenberger, Grounding and Necessity
summary: PDF p. 19 (article p.16), section III: Leuenberger's proposed blocker-blocker case retains the original facts while changing what is required for their grounding role. It tests persistence of the full-ground relation despite their truth. It is not by itself a case where the selected grounds hold and the target is false. PDF p. 20 (article p.17), Supervenience of Grounding: The proposed supervenience claim compares worlds agreeing on all obtaining facts. The case compares selected complete-ground facts across worlds which can differ elsewhere, so restricting the agreement to that record requires a locality premise not given by the proposed principle. PDF p. 8 (article p.5), Entailment, Factivity, Internality: The source distinguishes modal consequence for the target from preservation of grounding when its relata both hold. The route can use joint necessitation without warranting internality; carrying the same ground assignment across worlds needs the separate persistence condition.
